::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Feb 26th 1880  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne,Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS University of Iowa; MsL/Y56/1880
:::

My dear [Florence](people/person_1520.qmd)

You have a birthday so seldom that one recollects it, so pray accept my best wishes and this tiny book.[^1] I am afraid there is a little black speck on its cover, but do not look to reject it on that account I hope you received the second volume of [Thrupp on the Psalms](other_books/otherbook_928.qmd). I do not like all of him, though I have learnt a great deal from him, he does not tread in the beaten lines. 

I hope this warmer weather is refreshing you, it has brought up a great crowd of snow drops, and some primroses, but the Lent Lilies lag behind Lent.

With love to [your sister](people/person_1519.qmd), and kind regards to [the General](people/person_1521.qmd)

Yours affectionately
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: 1880 was a leap year, and Wilford's birthday was evidently on the 29 February.
